question: The ‘Tattvarthadhigamasutra’, regarded as the first book on Jaina philosophy, was authored by _______
solution:
The correct answer is __**Umasvati**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **The 'Tattvarthadhigamasutra'** is regarded as the first authoritative text on **Jaina philosophy**. It is considered a foundational scripture for both the **Svetambara** and **Digambara** sects of Jainism. 
• The text was authored by **Umasvati**, also known as **Umasvami**, a renowned Jain scholar. He lived around the 2nd to 3rd century CE, making this text a pivotal work of Jain literature. 
• The Tattvarthadhigamasutra is written in **Sanskrit** and is structured as an aphoristic text, making it concise yet comprehensive in elucidating Jain philosophy and doctrine. 
• The book systematically explains the **seven fundamental truths (Tattvas)** in Jainism, including concepts like right faith, right knowledge, and right conduct, which are critical for liberation (Moksha). 
• It is one of the few Jain texts written in Sanskrit, as most Jain scriptures are traditionally in **Prakrit**. Its use of Sanskrit allowed it to reach a broader intellectual audience in ancient India. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Umasvati and His Contributions:** 
• Umasvati is considered a unifying figure in Jainism, as his work is respected by both major sects of Jainism: **Svetambara** and **Digambara**. 
• He is believed to have been born in the Kushan Empire era and is credited with making Jain philosophy accessible to a scholarly audience. 
• **Content of the Tattvarthadhigamasutra:** 
• The text is divided into **10 chapters**, dealing with topics such as the nature of reality, the soul, karma, and liberation. 
• It outlines the path of **three jewels** (Ratnatraya) in Jainism: **Samyak Darshana (Right Faith), Samyak Jnana (Right Knowledge),** and **Samyak Charitra (Right Conduct)**. 
• **Importance of the Tattvarthadhigamasutra:** 
• It serves as a bridge between Jain philosophy and mainstream Indian philosophical thought, engaging with concepts like the **nature of the soul and metaphysics**. 
• The text has been extensively commented on by later Jain scholars, which further expanded its influence and interpretation. 
• **Other Options Explained:** 
• **Mahavira:** Mahavira is the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism and is credited with organizing Jain teachings into a structured form but did not author the Tattvarthadhigamasutra. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.*** 
• **Bhadrabahu:** Bhadrabahu was a Jain monk and scholar, known for his role in preserving Jain texts and traditions, but he was not the author of this text. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.*** 
• **Rishabhadeva:** Rishabhadeva, or Lord Rishabha, is the first Tirthankara of Jainism, revered for introducing the concept of asceticism, but he is not associated with the Tattvarthadhigamasutra. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.*** 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Jain Philosophy:** Jainism emphasizes the principles of **Ahimsa (non-violence), Aparigraha (non-possessiveness),** and **Satya (truthfulness)**, forming the ethical core of the religion. 
• **Karma in Jainism:** Jainism presents a unique perspective on karma, viewing it as a material substance that binds to the soul due to actions, and liberation is achieved by shedding this karma. 
• **Role of Tirthankaras:** The Tirthankaras are spiritual teachers who achieve liberation and help guide others on the path to Moksha. Mahavira is the most prominent among them. 
• **Canonical Texts:** Jain scriptures are divided into two categories: **Agamas** (canonical texts) and **Non-Agamas** (commentaries and other works). The Tattvarthadhigamasutra falls into the latter category. </ul
